judgment.rationale: Both endpoints are P2 (rank 1) Skills Objectives, so the same-grain and same-rank conditions are met and direction needs substantive evidence. The first SFI is a whole-number computation skill ('Divide numbers less than or equal to 60 by 6', Unit 3, Whole Numbers, Key Unit Competence covering multiply and divide 0-1000). The shared Grade ancestor and the single shared token 'division' alone were not treated as sufficient; the pair-specific computation-to-application link carries the judgment. The first states 'Count, read, and write numbers less than or equal to 2000' (LCs: count/read/write numbers ≤2000); the second requires dividing a 4-digit number by a single-digit number with dividend not exceeding 2000. Fluent counting, reading and writing of numerals within the same 0–2000 range is the number-representation proficiency operated on when dividing within that range, so proficiency in the first substantively supports success in the second, while the reverse is not supported.
